model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 seat, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over Ricardo Cabrera, with markets pricing her around 96%. With no polling available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower race or a surge of outside spending for Cabrera would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, is favored to win a second full term in this San Diego-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. She advanced to the general against Republican Ricardo Cabrera, a non-incumbent challenger with no reported fundraising. Jacobs has raised about $1.6 million and holds a cash advantage, with modest outside support and no recorded opposition spending.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Markets price Jacobs at roughly 96%, consistent with a comfortable but not automatic win in the low-twenties margin range.
